standoff.text: A stalemate or deadlock between two equally matched opponents.

sweatshop.text: A factory where workers are employed for long hours at low wages.

touchstone.text: A standard or criterion by which something is judged.

trapdoor.text: A hinged or removable panel in a floor, ceiling, or roof.

treadmill.text: A device for exercise; a job or situation that is tiring or boring.

underdog.text: A competitor thought to have little chance of winning.

watchdog.text: A dog kept to guard property; a person or group monitoring practices.

watershed.text: An area separating waters flowing into different rivers; a turning point.

wildfire.text: A large destructive fire that spreads quickly.

windfall.text: A piece of unexpected good fortune; fruit blown down by the wind.

wonderland.text: A land or place full of wonderful things.

workhorse.text: A horse used for work; a person or machine that dependably performs hard work.

cyberattack.text: An attempt by hackers to damage or destroy a computer network.

ethernet.text: A system for connecting computers within a local area network.

fracking.text: Injecting liquid at high pressure into rock to extract oil or gas.

gasoline.text: A refined petroleum used as fuel for internal combustion engines.

joystick.text: A lever controlling the direction of an aircraft or a video game character.

brainchild.text: An idea or invention originating with a particular person.

dictaphone.text: A trademarked machine for recording speech for transcription.

headhunter.text: A person who identifies and approaches suitable candidates for jobs; a person who collects heads.

infographic.text: A visual image such as a chart used to represent information.

micromanage.text: To control every part of a group's work, however small.

mogul.text: An important or powerful person; a bump on a ski slope.

pinstripe.text: A very narrow stripe in cloth, typical of formal suits.

pitchman.text: A person who delivers a sales pitch.

publicist.text: A person responsible for publicizing a product or person.

stenography.text: The action or process of writing in shorthand.

synergy.text: The interaction of elements that produces a combined effect greater than their sum.

telegraphist.text: A person who sends and receives telegraph messages.

webinar.text: A seminar conducted over the internet.

whistleblower.text: A person who exposes illicit activity within an organization.

bandolier.text: A shoulder belt with loops for cartridges.

boomtown.text: A town undergoing rapid growth due to sudden prosperity.

buckshot.text: Coarse lead shot used in shotgun shells.

buffalo.text: A bison; a heavily built wild ox.

cattleman.text: A person who tends or rears cattle.

chaps.text: Leather leggings worn by cowboys; men or boys.

corral.text: A pen for livestock on a farm or ranch.

derringer.text: A small pistol with a large bore.

fishhook.text: A barbed hook for catching fish.

frontiersman.text: A man living in the region of a frontier.

gallows.text: A structure for hanging a person.

gunfight.text: A fight involving an exchange of gunfire.

gunpowder.text: An explosive consisting of saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal.

homestead.text: A house with outbuildings; land granted to a settler.

horseshoe.text: A U-shaped iron plate nailed to a horse's hoof.

knapsack.text: A bag with shoulder straps carried on the back.

lariat.text: A rope used as a lasso or for tethering.

lasso.text: A rope with a noose at one end, used for catching cattle.

lawman.text: A law enforcement officer, especially a sheriff.

longhorn.text: An animal of a breed of cattle with very long horns.

lynching.text: The killing of someone by a mob without legal trial.

mustang.text: A small, lightly built feral horse.

packhorse.text: A horse used to carry loads.

quicksilver.text: Liquid mercury; moving or changing rapidly.

saddlebag.text: A bag attached to a saddle.

sagebrush.text: An aromatic shrub of arid regions of western North America.

sheriff.text: An elected officer in a county responsible for keeping the peace.

snowshoe.text: A flat device attached to a boot for walking on snow.

spurs.text: Devices with a small spike worn on a rider's heel.

stampede.text: A sudden panicked rush of a number of horses or cattle.

trapper.text: A person who traps wild animals for their fur.

varmint.text: A troublesome wild animal; a troublesome person.

babysitting.text: Looking after a child while the parents are out.

buggy.text: A small horse-drawn carriage; a pushchair; adjective: full of bugs.

clubhouse.text: A building used by a club; a children's den.

dummy.text: A model of a human being; a pacifier (British); a stupid person.

firstborn.text: The first child born to parents.

homeschooling.text: The education of children at home.

kiddo.text: A friendly or familiar form of address for a child.

latchkey.text: A key to an outer door; describing a child left alone after school.

lunchbox.text: A container for carrying a packed lunch.

matchbox.text: A small box in which matches are sold.

pacifier.text: A rubber or plastic nipple for a baby to suck on.

paddling.text: Walking with bare feet in shallow water.

piggyback.text: A ride on someone's back and shoulders.

playdate.text: A date arranged by parents for children to play together.

playhouse.text: A toy house for children to play in; a theater.

playpen.text: A small portable enclosure in which a baby or small child can play safely.

pram.text: A four-wheeled carriage for a baby (British).

pushchair.text: A folding chair on wheels in which a young child is pushed along (British).

rompers.text: A one-piece garment for a young child.

sandbox.text: A shallow box filled with sand for children to play in.

sandcastle.text: A model of a castle built in sand.

schoolyard.text: The grounds of a school, used for play.

seesaw.text: A long plank balanced in the middle for children to ride up and down.

snowman.text: A figure resembling a person, made from compressed snow.

teething.text: The process of growing one's first teeth.

tricycle.text: A vehicle similar to a bicycle but with three wheels.
